title: Build a multidimensional life
excerpt: Make room for positive emotion, deep engagement, strong relationships, meaning, and accomplishment. A good life should not be reduced to a single metric.

title: Seek new information, keep your values clear
excerpt: Seek new people, ideas, stories, and experiences that can challenge, reinforce, or update your worldview. Let your beliefs remain flexible, but let your core values provide a stable basis for action.
source: Julia Galef; Acceptance and Commitment Therapy

title: Ask your future self before sacrificing the present
excerpt: When sacrificing the present for the future, ask yourself if your future self would agree with the decision or tell you not to make that sacrifice.

title: Learn to build and learn to sell
excerpt: Value must be created, understood, and chosen.

title: Choose long-term games with people you respect
excerpt: Choose long-term games with people you respect.

title: Protect your attention
excerpt: What repeatedly captures your attention eventually shapes your life.

title: Own equity, not just your time
excerpt: You are not going to get rich renting out your time. You must own equity, a piece of a business, to gain your financial freedom.

title: Do not use risk to regain control during crisis
excerpt: Do not engage in impulsive or risky activity as a way to regain control over your life during times of crisis.

title: Making hard decisions is impossible without knowing your values
excerpt: Many decisions are values-limited, not information-limited; clear priorities make hard choices less hard.

title: Do not mistake shadows for reality
excerpt: Familiar appearances and expectations can feel like the whole world; growth requires the uncomfortable turn toward clearer understanding.

title: Know yourself, then choose who you become
excerpt: Self-knowledge keeps aspiration honest, but a decision is also a commitment to the person you want to become.

title: Not all choices have to be practical
excerpt: Practical benefits can be real without being the reason an activity matters; challenge, agency, and participation are reasons of their own, but only when the sacrifice fits your priorities.

title: Value people who have examined their values
excerpt: People who challenge your values are valuable when they have examined their own and are open to good-faith discussion; they can be sparring partners for better ideas. Avoid people who tell you how to live while refusing discussion or debate.

title: Endurance is not alignment
excerpt: Repeatedly tolerating a misaligned relationship or job can dull your sense that something is wrong until you lose trust in your own judgment.

title: Address primal impulses without being controlled by them
excerpt: Primal impulses must be addressed, but they should not control you. Evolutionary psychology can explain desire without telling you what is worth wanting; if every decision is justified by satisfying those desires, you have turned yourself into an ape.

title: Choose your values before others choose them for you
excerpt: Societal values, primal impulses, and other people's expectations can quietly set your priorities around desirability, status, money, and comfort; examine and choose values of your own.

title: Build values beyond instinct and inheritance
excerpt: Personal values should balance primal instincts and inherited norms, guide difficult decisions, and evolve through lived experience and reflection.

title: Clarity is useful without being complete
excerpt: A simplified worldview can make action easier, but usefulness is not the same as truth and nuance can create internal conflict.

title: Avoid sloth
excerpt: Every once in a while, do something that scares you; you cannot choose the same fear forever, because eventually it will stop being frightening. Comfort rots you from the inside out.
